questions.question: What is a stanza of four lines called?
questions.explanation: A quatrain has four lines, a couplet two and a tercet three. A sonnet is a complete 14-line poem form.

questions.question: What is enjambment?
options: When a sentence flows across a line break without pause
A pause at the end of every line
questions.explanation: Enjambment is when the sentence continues over the line break, in contrast to end-stopped lines that pause at the line end.

questions.question: What is iambic pentameter?
options: A line of five iambs (da-DUM) — the most important metre in English poetry
A rhyme scheme with five rhymes
questions.explanation: Iambic pentameter has five iambs (unstressed-stressed) per line and is the most important metre in English poetry.

questions.question: Which device is used in "The wind whispered through the trees"?
questions.explanation: Giving the wind the human ability to whisper is personification. A simile would use "like" or "as".

questions.question: What is the difference between alliteration and assonance?
options: Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds; assonance repeats vowel sounds
Alliteration repeats vowels; assonance repeats consonants
questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds ("silent sea"), while assonance repeats vowel sounds within words.
